rows.selection_reason: No completed experiments exist, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal baseline is competitive before testing multiprofile, advanced encoders, or fusion. config_001 tests the simplest RNA-only, single-profile PCA setting, establishing a reference validation accuracy/F1 and isolating the RNA representation/profile baseline. It is the best next experiment because it is low-risk, avoids confounding multiple design choices, and creates an anchor for later comparisons of RNA encoders, aggregation, and multimodal fusion under a limited budget.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline, so the major uncertainty is whether the image modality provides useful signal at all. Testing image-only ResNet50 single-profile establishes a simple unimodal image baseline without assuming multimodal or more complex designs will help. This is the best next experiment because it directly compares the two main modalities, uses a simple model to reduce confounding, and creates a necessary reference for later multimodal fusion experiments.

Existing evidence is sparse but points to RNA as the stronger modality: RNA-only PCA single-profile achieves 0.485 validation accuracy and 0.464 F1, while image-only ResNet single-profile is much weaker at 0.208 accuracy and 0.172 F1. The main uncertainty is whether the current RNA-only baseline can be improved by using multiple profiles and a simple aggregation strategy. config_002 tests this by keeping the same promising RNA encoder, pca_n2000, and only extending from single-profile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation. This is a logical, low-confounding extension of the best current result, and avgpool is preferred over transformer as the simpler baseline aggregation. It is the best next use of budget because it directly clarifies whether profile aggregation matters before investing in more complex multimodal or learned-encoder configurations.

RNA PCA multiprofile with avgpool is currently best (0.591 acc / 0.573 F1), clearly above singleprofile RNA (0.485) and image-only ResNet (0.208). The main remaining uncertainty in this promising direction is whether transformer aggregation can outperform avgpool for multiprofile RNA. config_003 changes only aggregation from config_002, isolating that effect and directly extending the best configuration. It is a high-value next experiment because it can improve the current best RNA-only model and will inform whether transformer aggregation should be used in later multimodal settings without introducing multiple confounding changes.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool, which outperforms single-profile RNA and transformer aggregation. Image-only ResNet is weak, so adding multimodality is not yet justified. The most informative next step is to test whether a stronger learned RNA representation improves on PCA while keeping the validated multiprofile/avgpool setting. config_008 changes only the RNA encoder to scGPT, isolating the representation choice and exploiting the current best direction.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA, which outperforms transformer aggregation and scGPT avgpool. The main uncertainty is whether the untested scVI RNA representation can improve on PCA/scGPT under this same strong setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder relative to the best RNA-only setup, cleanly isolating the representation effect. This is an efficient next experiment because it exploits the promising multiprofile+avgpool direction, may identify a better RNA base for later multimodal tests, and avoids confounding the result by adding image fusion at the same time.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool is the best RNA-only setup so far (acc 0.650, F1 0.628), while transformer aggregation was worse than avgpool for pca. config_006 tests whether transformer aggregation can improve the best scvi multiprofile configuration or confirms avgpool as the better aggregation. It is the best next step because it is a one-factor extension of the current best, reduces uncertainty about aggregation before adding image/fusion complexity, and avoids changing multiple design choices at once.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA multiprofile with scvi_n200 is the best representation, with transformer aggregation slightly ahead of avgpool (config_006: 0.653 acc, 0.628 F1), while image-only ResNet is weak (config_010: 0.208 acc). The main uncertainty is whether adding image information to the best RNA pipeline can improve validation accuracy through fusion. config_032 keeps the best RNA encoder, multiprofile setting, and transformer aggregation, and adds the already-evaluated ResNet image encoder with the simplest concat fusion. This makes it a minimal multimodal extension of config_006, helping isolate the effect of adding image features/fusion without introducing untested ViT or weighted-fusion complexity. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest RNA evidence while directly testing whether multimodal fusion adds value.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, scVI, ResNet50, transformer, concat) with acc 0.688, but this is a single multimodal result and only modestly better than the best RNA-only model. Image-only evidence is sparse and weak for single-profile ResNet50 (acc 0.208), so it is unclear whether the multimodal gain comes from useful multiprofile image features or from complementary RNA-image fusion. config_012 tests the exact image-side counterpart of config_032 without RNA, isolating the contribution of multiprofile ResNet50 image representation. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces a key uncertainty before committing to more multimodal variants: if image-only multiprofile is weak, it supports the multimodal direction; if it is strong, it redirects attention to image representation/aggregation rather than fusion.

The strongest result so far is config_032, a multimodal multiprofile model using scvi_n200, ResNet50, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion, with validation accuracy 0.6878 and F1 0.6585, clearly above the best RNA-only scvi_n200 transformer model at 0.6530. This suggests the current representation, profile setting, aggregation, and image modality are promising, but fusion strategy has not been isolated because only concat has been tested in the best configuration. config_033 changes only the fusion method from concat to weighted while keeping the rest of the best setup fixed, so it directly tests whether weighted fusion can improve performance or whether concat is already sufficient. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest evidence, avoids changing multiple factors at once, and reduces uncertainty about an important design choice under a limited budget.
